clue.text: Great spelling

definitions.meaning: informal praise, as in 'that's wonderful, brilliant'

explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' reads as orthography but here means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: colloquial approval of something excellent, and the art of enchantment practised by wizards.

clue.text: Lose track of rodents crossing mountains, going up?

indicators.note: crossing means the rodents' word stretches across, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: going up, in a down clue, means the mountains' word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Alps are a range of mountains

explanation.surface: You might lose sight of mice clambering over the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'going up' means reading from bottom to top, so the mountains' word is reversed before 'crossing' wraps the rodents around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in the wrong place and so lose it is to mislay, losing track of where it is.

clue.text: Grand noise surrounding one, right? Grand? It's belting!

indicators.note: surrounding means the outer word's letters go round the inner ones

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
din means a loud noise
G again for grand
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An excited reviewer calls a piece grand, noisy and belting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts I and R inside G-DIN-G, after the first G. 'Belting' reads as loud or excellent, but means putting a belt on.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird is to fasten a belt or sash round the waist, so fastening one on is belting.

clue.text: Basket of game

definitions.meaning: a manger or baby's cot, sometimes a wicker bed
short for cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard

explanation.definitionFit: A baby's cot or manger, sometimes woven like a basket, is one sense; the card game cribbage, shortened, is the other.

clue.text: Period for deliveries which should get extra?

definitions.text: Period for deliveries which should get extra?

parts.words: Period for deliveries which should get extra?
parts.note: in cricket a set of six deliveries is an over, so a span of time for bowling them is read whimsically; the real sense is extra hours worked that earn extra pay

explanation.surface: A courier wonders which delivery slot should earn a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled, so 'deliveries' points to bowling, not post. Cricket also has 'extras', runs not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours worked beyond the normal shift are paid at a higher rate, a period that gets extra money.

clue.text: Money for new business: speculation on London, maybe?

parts.note: a venture is a speculative undertaking
London is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: Investors put funds into start-ups, a speculative bet on the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds invested in a new, risky enterprise in return for a share of it are the money backing start-ups.

clue.text: Went on horseback, we hear, to make highway

indicators.note: we hear means a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: rode means went on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider travelled on horseback to make a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A highway is a main route for traffic, a synonym in general usage.

clue.text: Pretend I will get publication in English

parts.note: mag, a magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: Pretend I'll get my article printed in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To make believe, as children do in play, is to conjure a scenario in the mind.

clue.text: Modem/AI link-up incorporates communication method

indicators.note: incorporates means the clue text holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Linking a modem with AI brings in a new way of communicating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' signals letters running across ModEM/AI Link.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail sent over a network is a common method of communicating.

clue.text: Exaggerate 'Lioness eats Ian' when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline sensationally reporting a lioness eating a man named Ian.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting a story in a lurid, overblown way to provoke excitement is overstating it.

clue.text: Diners upset about a fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the a
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of diners are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restaurant customers complain about a fish dish they were served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DINERS into SRDINE, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, usually tinned, is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Artist, once more back in front, falls

indicators.note: in front places the turned word before the artist's letters
back means the word for once more is read backwards

parts.note: once more means again
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter returns to the front of the queue once again before falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb but is the noun for a waterfall; RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the border of the US state of New York and Ontario, Canada, are named by the plural noun.

clue.text: Look, trendy item to do 2 with?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: Look at this fashionable thing you could wear for the 2 clue!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sends you to 2-down: the idiom is to gird up one's loins, readying oneself for action.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about preparing for action, it is the lower back region of the body that one girds up.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point of difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: A difficulty under discussion is one sense; the legal word for a person's offspring or descendants is the other.

clue.text: Call and help returning Liberal

indicators.note: returning means the word for help comes back, read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Phoning a Liberal politician who is coming back to offer help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone on the telephone is to make a call, from the rotary disc once spun to enter a number.

clue.text: Doctor, I have to be at the wheel

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A doctor says she has to take the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the steering wheel means controlling a car, operating the vehicle.

clue.text: Fellow's cottage finally becoming minister's residence

parts.note: man's means the fellow's

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word cottage

explanation.surface: A man's cottage ends up becoming the vicar's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The house provided for a Presbyterian or Scottish church minister is the term for that official residence.

clue.text: Thin material used for tabs?

parts.note: tabs is northern British slang for cigarettes, and the thin sheet used to roll one is meant; the surface suggests tabs as labels or tags on folders

explanation.surface: Asking what flimsy stuff is used to make the little tags on files.
explanation.walkthrough: Tabs looks like labels on files, but in northern British slang a tab is a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers roll loose tobacco in a very thin sheet of paper made for the purpose.

clue.text: Train: concerning transport for those who are late?

parts.note: re means concerning, about

parts.words: transport for those who are late
parts.note: the late are the dead, and a hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin

explanation.surface: A rail notice about transport laid on for latecomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun, but is the verb to practise. 'the late' means the dead, not the tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play or piece before performance is to train for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Time off: go to get face bones reset

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: reset means put back in a new arrangement, as broken bones are set, so the letters of face bones are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient takes time off work to have broken facial bones set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' turns FACE BONES into OFABSENCE; the medical surface makes 'reset' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal permission to be away from work or duty for a period is a spell of time away from the job.

clue.text: Question about king supporting eastern attendant

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, means the following piece sits beneath, so the eastern letter comes first
about means the question's word goes round the king's letter

parts.note: a query is a question
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A query about whether the king backs an attendant from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside QUERY to make QUERRY, and 'supporting' places it below E in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the royal household who personally attends a member of the royal family is a court attendant.

clue.text: Liquid derived from hash plant, neither large nor small

indicators.note: derived from means the letters are reworked from the source
neither, with nor, means both the following letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A liquid extracted from cannabis comes in neither large nor small sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither large nor small' drops L and S from HASH PLANT to leave HAHPANT, which 'derived from' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable oil distilled from coal tar or petroleum, used as a solvent, is a liquid.

clue.text: Savage married a posh student

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A wedded, upper-class student is attacked viciously.
explanation.walkthrough: U is upper-class usage in British English; L is the learner plate shown by student drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack fiercely and wound, as a big cat or dog does, is to savage someone; both are verbs.

clue.text: Bird initially making a sound like a crow

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A bird starts making a crow-like call.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Mother, mostly pleasant, is very busy

parts.note: ma means mother

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Mum is generally nice but is rushed off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of NICE to leave NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantically energetic and hectic, as in a frenzied day, is the informal adjectival sense.

clue.text: A footnote on English recess

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: An English textbook has a footnote about a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a school holiday but is an architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular vaulted alcove at the east end of a church is a recess in the building.

clue.text: Jumper seen in sort of market?

definitions.meaning: a small leaping insect, not a sweater
a street market selling secondhand goods, so named after the insect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British jumper, a sweater, but means a creature that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingless bloodsucking insect famous for leaping is one sense; it also names a market of old and used goods.

clue.text: Advertise electrical accessory

definitions.meaning: to promote something by mentioning it publicly
the pronged fitting on a cable that goes into a socket

explanation.definitionFit: Promoting a product with a favourable mention is one sense; the pronged connector that goes into a wall socket is the other.

clue.text: Composer and men in small room beginning to improvise

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for a small room

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A composer and his men cram into a tiny room to start improvising.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the army's term for enlisted men. 'in' puts OR in CELL to make CORELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concerti grossi, a composer of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Every second on pitch like a great show?

parts.note: all means every one
pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: Every second spent on the football pitch felt like a great show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports ground but is the substance tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A show whose cast is made up entirely of famous performers is described with this adjective, hence great.

clue.text: Traveller reportedly much more pretty

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard as said, not as written

parts.note: way fairer, in informal speech, means much prettier

explanation.surface: A wanderer is said to be far better looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is colloquial for 'much', so 'much more pretty' is 'way fairer', which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who journeys on foot along roads is a traveller, an old literary word.

clue.text: Eat constantly — from scratch?

definitions.meaning: to snack little and often through the day, as cattle crop grass
a light scrape on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is just a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbling throughout the day like a grazing animal is one sense; a superficial wound where skin is scraped is the other.
